case_title: Tanua Rabidas v. State of Assam
accused_occupation: Assistant in the Social Welfare Department
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under section 302 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/-
neutral_facts: The accused, along with a co-accused, were present in the house on the day of the incident. The accused poured kerosene oil on his wife and set her on fire. The victim was taken to the hospital where she succumbed to burn injuries. The victim's brother lodged an FIR. A dying declaration was made by the victim in the presence of a doctor and a nurse, stating that her husband had set her on fire. The doctor and nurse's statements were corroborated by the victim's brother and another witness who accompanied him to the hospital. The prosecution case relied on the dying declaration, medical evidence, and eyewitness accounts to establish the accused's guilt.
